headers.//: The city, and 90% of what a visit costs. Every one of these is requested with ?v=<stamp>, and the stamp is the glb's mtime, so the URL changes exactly when the bytes do. That is what makes immutable safe: a re-export is a new URL, not a stale cache. Without this a refresh re-downloads 6 MB.

The one file that carries the stamp cannot be keyed on it. main.js already asks for it with cache: no-store; this says the same thing to every proxy in between, because a cached copy of this file pins the whole page to an old deploy.
Decoder builds, versioned by their own contents upstream and never edited here.
The card and the icons: not versioned, so a day, and stale-while-revalidate so replacing one is never a cold fetch for anybody.
Nothing here is embeddable and nothing here takes input, so the page says so.
